public_rationale: The evidence supports concern about unreliable checking, including failures when tools are available. But it also shows useful factual verification and successful detection of selected reasoning mistakes. AVeriTeC's 63% score combines verdicts with evidence quality and cannot be read as a failure rate on basic checks. METR documents both unsupported conclusions and successful prompted detection. These findings do not settle the contextual claim that contemporary LLMs cannot dependably perform basic checking. They also do not establish a general lack of resourcefulness. Calling the claim contradicted merely because some checks succeed would apply an unfairly literal reading.

our_interpretation: In context, the ordinary reading concerns dependable checking, rather than an inability to perform any successful check.

Basic fact checking means verifying straightforward factual claims against available evidence. Sanity checking means detecting obvious errors, inconsistencies or unsupported conclusions, including in the system's own work.
External sources, retrieval, calculators, code and checking workflows are allowed. Marcus did not restrict the claim to unaided self-correction.

The observation concerns systems contemporary with the post. Because research has no regular reporting quarter, use the latest completed calendar year and the elapsed publication year, January 2024 through January 13, 2025, as the recent evaluation period.
Treat resourcefulness as the practical ability to use available information and methods to check an answer. Checking failures alone cannot establish a general absence of that ability.
Neither isolated failures nor isolated successes settle the reliability claim.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of contemporary LLMs show substantial recurring failures to verify straightforward facts and detect obvious inconsistencies, including when ordinary external verification is available. The failures must concern checking itself, rather than merely producing an initially incorrect answer.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reproducible evaluations show dependable factual verification and obvious-error detection across varied basic tasks using ordinary resources. Success on selected examples or improvement over a weak baseline is insufficient.

ProCo improves checking and correction across factual question answering, arithmetic and commonsense tasks. Improvement establishes useful ability, but does not establish dependable performance across basic checks or resolve the broader resourcefulness inference.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reproducible evaluation of target-period model versions on varied, clearly basic factual and consistency checks, allowing ordinary retrieval and tools, reporting missed errors and false alarms, and including a comparable human baseline. It should distinguish detecting an error from correcting one identified by a human.
